translations.meta_description: A reputação gastronômica de Penang é construída com base em seus vendedores ambulantes durante o dia, mas a ilha se destaca depois de anoitecer. O mercado noturno em Batu Ferringhi brilha com fogueiras a carvão. O centro de vendedores ambulantes de Gurney Drive h
translations.content_markdown:
A sessão noturna é o serviço principal. As melhores barracas abrem às 17h e servem continuamente até esgotar, o que geralmente acontece por volta das 20h para os itens mais populares. O segundo turno de barracas abre às 19h e funciona até às 23h. Planeie chegar às 17h30 para apanhar o primeiro turno sem as filas mais longas.

**Frutos do mar na churrasqueira** é uma oferta exclusiva do período noturno em Gurney Drive. As barracas no lado voltado para o mar montam churrasqueiras a carvão à noite e exibem peixes frescos, camarões e lulas no gelo. A lula grelhada recheada com sambal é a melhor opção. O tostado por fora e o recheio agridoce criam uma combinação que vale a espera de 15 minutos.

**Wan tan mee** na Rua Chulia é o favorito da noite. A barraca no Kedai Kopi Heng Huat serve uma versão seca com molho de soja escura, *char siew* e bolinhos *wantan* numa tigela separada de caldo. Os noodles são elásticos. O *char siew* é caramelizado nos rebordos. Os *wantan* são recheados com uma mistura de porco e camarão. RM 6. A barraca abre às 18h e serve até à meia-noite.

**Roti canai** está disponível tarde na Chulia Street numa barraca mamak que funciona das 19h às 3h. O roti é mais fino e mais crocante do que o padrão, feito com uma proporção maior de óleo na massa. O dal que vem com ele é temperado com cominhos e sementes de mostarda preta. A barraca também serve roti telur (com ovo) e roti bom (com leite condensado).

**Frutos do mar grelhados** em Batu Ferringhi são a principal atração. Peixes, camarões, lulas e lagostas são exibidos no gelo e grelhados em carvão. A arraia (ikan pari) é a escolha mais confiável. Ela é besuntada com sambal, embrulhada em folha de bananeira e grelhada até que a carne se solte em lascas. O sambal da barraca mais próxima do acesso à praia é feito com chilli fresco e tem um ardor intenso, vibrante e limpo.

Gurney Drive é a opção noturna mais fácil para visitantes de primeira viagem. O centro de vendedores ambulantes é compacto, as barracas são identificadas, e a variedade significa que você pode experimentar vários pratos em uma única sentada. Chegue às 17h30 para evitar as maiores filas.

A cena gastronômica noturna de Penang está espalhada pela ilha, mas as distâncias são curtas. O passeio gastronômico noturno Simply Enak Penang abrange Gurney Drive e a Rua Chulia em uma única noite, com um guia local que conhece os vendedores e sabe navegar pelas multidões noturnas.

title: Night Food Guide Malaysia: Where to Eat After Dark
excerpt: Malaysia's Night Food Scene Malaysia eats late. The hawker stalls that close at lunch are replaced in the evening by a different set of vendors.

children.text: Malaysia's Night Food Scene

Malaysia eats late. The hawker stalls that close at lunch are replaced in the evening by a different set of vendors. The pasar malam sets up as the sun goes down. The Mamak restaurants stay open until 3 AM. The supper culture here is not a late-night novelty. It is how the country feeds itself after dark.

For a first-time visitor, the night food scene is where Malaysia reveals itself most clearly. The daytime heat is gone. The crowds are different. The food is cooked over higher flames and served with more intensity. This guide covers the three main ways Malaysia eats after dark and where to experience each one.
Pasar Malam: The Mobile Night Market

Pasar malam are temporary night markets that operate on a rotating schedule. Each day of the week, a different neighbourhood hosts one. The stalls arrive in vans around 4 PM, set up quickly, and pack down by 10 PM.
The food at a pasar malam is designed for walking and eating. There are no tables. You buy, you eat, you move. The dishes are smaller than hawker centre portions and the prices are lower.
**What to eat at a pasar malam:**

**Apam balik** is a thick pancake folded over a filling of sweet corn, crushed peanuts, and sugar. The batter is cooked in a round cast-iron mould. The edges are thin and crisp. The centre is thick and soft. The filling is warm and sweet. Look for the stall with the longest queue. That is the one.

**Keropok lekor** is deep-fried fish sausage from the east coast. Made from mackerel and sago flour, shaped into rolls, boiled, sliced, and fried to order. The texture is chewy inside, crisp outside. Served with a sweet-spicy chilli dipping sauce. The keropok lekor stall at the Taman Connaught pasar malam in KL is the most famous.

**Satay** at a pasar malam is grilled over charcoal in full view. The smoke tells you where the stall is before you see it. Chicken and beef skewers, served with peanut sauce, cucumber, and ketupat. The grilling is done in small batches, so the skewers are always hot.

**Fried chicken** at a pasar malam is coated in a turmeric and rice flour batter and fried in deep oil. The skin is crisp. The meat stays juicy because the frying time is short and the oil is hot. Buy one piece and eat it while walking.

**Cendol** at a pasar malam is served from a stall with a hand-cranked ice shaver. The ice is fluffier than machine-shaved versions. The coconut milk is fresh. The gula melaka syrup is dark and slightly bitter.
**The best pasar malam:**
Taman Connaught, KL (Wednesday): the longest pasar malam in Malaysia, with over 700 stalls
Batu Ferringhi, Penang (nightly during peak season): a beachside night market with food and souvenirs
Jonker Street, Melaka (weekend evenings): a heritage street market in the old town
SS2, Petaling Jaya (Monday): a large pasar malam known for its food variety
Late-Night Hawker Centres

Some hawker centres operate a day shift and a night shift. The day shift vendors pack up around 4 PM, and the night shift vendors take over from 5 PM until midnight or later. Each shift has different stalls and different specialties.

**Gurney Drive Hawker Centre, Penang** is the most famous evening hawker centre in Malaysia. It operates from about 5 PM to 11 PM. The evening is the main service. The best stalls open at 5 PM and serve continuously until they sell out. The laksa, char kway teow, and Hokkien mee in the evening are made with more energy and higher heat than the daytime versions. The barbecue seafood stalls only operate in the evening, grilling fresh fish, prawns, and squid over charcoal.

**Jalan Alor, KL** is the city's most famous night food street. It operates from about 5 PM to 2 AM. The street is closed to traffic in the evening. Hawker stalls line both sides, with open-air seating in the middle. The food here is more Chinese than Malay: grilled fish, seafood, satay, and noodle dishes. The atmosphere is loud, smoky, and energetic. Jalan Alor is touristy, but the food quality is still high because the competition is fierce.

**Chulia Street, Penang** transforms into a late-night food corridor after 8 PM. The late session runs from 8 PM to midnight. The crowd is a mix of backpackers and local families. The Hokkien mee on Chulia Street is served by a stall that only opens in the evening. The broth has been simmering since 2 PM and the prawn shells have released their full flavour.
Supper Culture: Mamak Stalls and Nasi Kandar

The Mamak stall is the backbone of Malaysia's late-night food scene. Mamak restaurants are Indian-Muslim establishments that operate 24 hours a day or until well past midnight. They are found on almost every major road in every Malaysian city.

Mamak food is designed for any time of day or night. **Roti canai** is the most popular late-night order. The dough is stretched thin, folded, and cooked on a flat grill. It takes five minutes. Eat it with dal or curry. **Murtabak** is the stuffed version: minced beef, egg, and onion folded into the stretched dough and fried until golden. **Mee goreng** is fried noodles with soy sauce, chilli, egg, and vegetables.
**Teh tarik** is the standard Mamak drink at any hour. Pulled milk tea, sweet and creamy. It is served in a glass and the foam on top is the sign of a well-made version.

Nasi kandar stalls also operate late in Penang. **Line Clear Restaurant** on Lebuh Penang in George Town is open 24 hours. Rice with curries, fried chicken, and vegetables. The fish curry at 2 AM hits differently than the lunchtime version. The flavours have had hours to develop.
What to Eat at Night That You Cannot Eat During the Day
Some dishes are evening-only offerings. The vendors who make them do not operate during the day.

**Barbecue seafood** is an evening-only dish at most hawker centres. Fresh fish, prawns, and squid are marinated in a spice paste and grilled over charcoal. The flavour is smoky, the texture is firm, and the sambal topping adds heat. The grilled stingray (ikan pari) with sambal is the best option.

**Ikan bakar** (grilled fish) is wrapped in banana leaf with spices and grilled over charcoal. The fish stays moist while the spices form a crust. It is an evening dish because the charcoal grills are only set up after the afternoon heat has passed.
**Satay** in the evening is made with smaller batches and fresher grilling than the daytime versions. The charcoal gives the meat a smoky flavour that gas grills cannot reproduce.

**Fried banana (pisang goreng)** at a night market is made to order. The batter is thin, the bananas are ripe, and the frying is done in small batches. The contrast between the crispy outside and the soft, sweet inside is best when the fritters are fresh from the oil.
The Bottom Line

Malaysia's night food scene is one of the best in Southeast Asia because the country never stops cooking. The pasar malam feed entire neighbourhoods. The hawker centres switch shifts and keep serving. The Mamak stalls stay open until sunrise.

The key to eating well at night in Malaysia is to follow the crowds. The stall with a queue at 10 PM is the stall to eat at. The pasar malam with the most people is the one to visit. The Mamak stall with the most tables occupied at 1 AM is serving the food that locals know is worth staying up for.

The Simply Enak food tours in Malaysia include evening sessions at the hawker centres and pasar malam where the night food scene is at its best. A local guide who knows the vendors and the schedule can help you eat more and walk less.

translations.excerpt: Malaysia makan lambat. Gerai-gerai penjaja yang tutup semasa makan tengah hari digantikan pada waktu petang oleh kumpulan penjual yang berbeza. Pasar malam terbenam ketika matahari terbenam. Restoran Mamak terus dibuka sehingga
translations.content_markdown:
**Apam balik** ialah lempeng tebal yang dilipat berisi jagung manis, kacang tanah yang dihancurkan, dan gula. Adunan dimasak dalam acuan besi tuang berbentuk bulat. Tepinya nipis dan rangup. Bahagian tengahnya tebal dan lembut. Isinya hangat dan manis. Cari gerai dengan barisan paling panjang. Itulah gerai yang terbaik.

## Pusat Penjaja Lewat Malam

**Jalan Alor, KL** adalah jalan makan malam yang paling terkenal di kota ini. Ia beroperasi dari kira-kira pukul 5 petang hingga pukul 2 pagi. Jalan ini ditutup untuk lalu lintas pada waktu petang. Gerai penjaja berbaris di kedua-dua belah, dengan tempat duduk terbuka di tengah. Makanan di sini lebih kepada masakan Cina berbanding Melayu: ikan panggang, makanan laut, satay, dan hidangan mi. Suasananya hingar-bingar, berasap, dan bertenaga. Jalan Alor merupakan kawasan pelancong, tetapi kualiti makanannya masih tinggi kerana persaingannya sengit.

**Teh tarik** adalah minuman standard Mamak pada bila-bila masa. Teh susu yang diregangkan, manis dan berkrim. Ia dihidangkan dalam gelas dan buih di atasnya adalah petanda versi yang dibuat dengan baik.

## Kesimpulan

Lawatan makanan Simply Enak di Malaysia termasuk sesi petang di pusat penjaja dan pasar malam di mana suasana makanan malam berada pada tahap terbaik. Pemandu tempatan yang mengenali penjual dan jadual boleh membantu anda makan lebih banyak dan berjalan kurang.

translations.meta_title: 马来西亚的夜间美食
translations.meta_description: 马来西亚吃饭很晚。午餐时关闭的小贩摊位在晚上被不同的摊贩所取代。当太阳落山时，夜市就开始了。 Mamak 餐厅营业至
translations.content_markdown:
**Apam balik** 是一种厚实的煎饼，对折包入甜玉米、花生碎和糖做成的馅料。面糊在圆形的铸铁模具中煎制而成。饼的边缘薄而酥脆，中间厚而松软，馅料温热香甜。找排队最长的那家摊位准没错。

## 深夜小贩中心

**吉隆坡阿罗街**是这座城市最著名的夜间美食街。营业时间大约从下午5点到凌晨2点。傍晚时街道禁止车辆通行，街道两旁排满了小贩档口，中间设有露天座位。这里的食物以中式为主，马来风味较少：烤鱼、海鲜、沙爹和面食。街上的气氛喧闹、烟火气十足，充满活力。阿罗街虽然游客很多，但因为竞争激烈，食物质量依然很高。

**拉茶（Teh tarik）**是嘛嘛档任何时候的标准饮品。拉制奶茶，甜而不腻，口感丝滑。装在玻璃杯中饮用，杯顶的泡沫是制作精良的标志。

## 总结

马来西亚的 Simply Enak 美食之旅包含夜间的Hawker中心小贩中心和夜市参观时段，届时夜宵文化最为精彩。熟悉摊主和营业时间的当地导游可以让你多吃少走。

translations.excerpt: In Malaysia wird spät gegessen. Die Garküchen, die mittags schließen, werden abends von anderen Verkäufern abgelöst. Der Pasar Malam öffnet bei Sonnenuntergang. Die Mamak-Restaurants haben bis tief in die Nacht geöffnet.

translations.content_markdown:
**Apam Balik** ist ein dicker Pfannkuchen, der über eine Füllung aus süßem Mais, zerdrückten Erdnüssen und Zucker gefaltet wird. Der Teig wird in einer runden Gusseisenform gebacken. Die Ränder sind dünn und knusprig. Die Mitte ist dick und weich. Die Füllung ist warm und süß. Sucht den Stand mit der längsten Schlange. Das ist der Richtige.

## Späte Nachtmärkte (Hawker Centres)

**Jalan Alor, KL** ist die berühmteste Nachtessenstraße der Stadt. Sie ist von etwa 17 Uhr bis 2 Uhr nachts geöffnet. Die Straße ist abends für den Verkehr gesperrt. Hawker-Stände reihen sich auf beiden Seiten, mit offenen Sitzgelegenheiten in der Mitte. Das Essen hier ist eher chinesisch als malaiisch: gegrillter Fisch, Meeresfrüchte, Satay und Nudelgerichte. Die Atmosphäre ist laut, rauchig und energiegeladen. Jalan Alor ist touristisch, aber die Qualität des Essens ist immer noch hoch, weil der Wettbewerb hart ist.

**Teh tarik** ist das Standardgetränk im Mamak zu jeder Stunde. Gezogener Milchtee, süß und cremig. Er wird in einem Glas serviert, und der Schaum oben ist das Zeichen für eine gut zubereitete Version.

## Das Fazit

Die Simply Enak Food-Touren in Malaysia beinhalten Abendsitzungen in den Hawker-Centern und Pasar Malam, wo die Nachtszenen für Essen am besten sind. Ein lokaler Guide, der die Verkäufer und den Zeitplan kennt, kann Ihnen helfen, mehr zu essen und weniger zu laufen.

El **Apam balik** es un panqueque grueso doblado sobre un relleno de maíz dulce, maní triturado y azúcar. La masa se cocina en un molde redondo de hierro fundido. Los bordes son finos y crujientes. El centro es grueso y suave. El relleno es cálido y dulce. Busca el puesto con la cola más larga. Ese es el indicado.

## Centros de comida nocturna

**Jalan Alor, KL** es la calle de comida nocturna más famosa de la ciudad. Opera desde aproximadamente las 5 PM hasta las 2 AM. La calle está cerrada al tráfico por la noche. Los puestos de vendedores ambulantes se alinean a ambos lados, con asientos al aire libre en el medio. La comida aquí es más china que malaya: pescado a la parrilla, mariscos, satay y platos de fideos. El ambiente es ruidoso, humeante y enérgico. Jalan Alor es turístico, pero la calidad de la comida sigue siendo alta porque la competencia es feroz.

**Teh tarik** es la bebida estándar de Mamak a cualquier hora. Té con leche estirado, dulce y cremoso. Se sirve en un vaso y la espuma en la parte superior es la señal de una versión bien hecha.

## La Conclusión

Los tours gastronómicos de Simply Enak en Malasia incluyen sesiones nocturnas en los *hawker centres* y *pasar malam*, donde la escena gastronómica nocturna está en su mejor momento. Un guía local que conoce a los vendedores y los horarios puede ayudarte a comer más y caminar menos.

**L'*apam balik*** est une crêpe épaisse pliée sur une garniture de maïs sucré, de cacahuètes concassées et de sucre. La pâte est cuite dans un moule rond en fonte. Les bords sont fins et croustillants. Le centre est épais et moelleux. La garniture est chaude et sucrée. Cherchez le stand avec la file d'attente la plus longue. C'est celui-là.

## Centres de restauration de nuit

**Jalan Alor, à Kuala Lumpur** est la rue gastronomique nocturne la plus célèbre de la ville. Elle fonctionne d'environ 17 heures à 2 heures du matin. La rue est fermée à la circulation en soirée. Des stands de hawkers bordent les deux côtés, avec des places assises en plein air au milieu. La cuisine y est davantage chinoise que malaise : poisson grillé, fruits de mer, satay et plats de nouilles. L'ambiance est bruyante, enfumée et énergique. Jalan Alor est touristique, mais la qualité de la nourriture reste élevée car la concurrence y est féroce.

Le **teh tarik** est la boisson standard des mamak à toute heure. Un thé au lait tiré, sucré et crémeux. Il est servi dans un verre et la mousse sur le dessus est le signe d'une préparation réussie.

## En conclusion

Les visites gastronomiques Simply Enak en Malaisie comprennent des sessions en soirée dans les hawker centres et les pasar malam où la scène culinaire nocturne est à son meilleur. Un guide local qui connaît les vendeurs et les horaires peut vous aider à manger plus et marcher moins.

translations.content_markdown:
**Apam balik** is een dikke pannenkoek die dubbelgevouwen wordt over een vulling van zoete maïs, gemalen pinda's en suiker. Het beslag wordt in een ronde gietijzeren vorm gebakken. De randen zijn dun en knapperig. Het midden is dik en zacht. De vulling is warm en zoet. Zoek het kraampje met de langste rij. Dat is dé juiste.

## Late-night eetkraampjes

**Jalan Alor, KL** is de beroemdste nachtelijke eetstraat van de stad. Het is geopend van ongeveer 17:00 tot 02:00. De straat is 's avonds afgesloten voor verkeer. Langs beide kanten staan hawkerkraampjes, met openluchtafdelingen in het midden. Het eten hier is meer Chinees dan Maleisisch: gegrilde vis, zeevruchten, saté en noedelgerechten. De sfeer is luidruchtig, rokerig en energiek. Jalan Alor is toeristisch, maar de kwaliteit van het eten is nog steeds hoog omdat de concurrentie hevig is.

**Teh tarik** is de standaard Mamak-drank op elk uur. Getrokken melkthee, zoet en romig. Het wordt geserveerd in een glas en het schuim bovenop is het kenmerk van een goed gemaakte versie.

## De Conclusie

De Simply Enak food tours in Maleisië omvatten avondsessies bij de hawkercentra en pasar malam, waar de nachtelijke eetscène op zijn popular is. Een lokale gids die de verkopers en het rooster kent, kan je helpen om meer te eten en minder te lopen.

**Apam balik**, это толстый блин, сложенный пополам с начинкой из сладкой кукурузы, дроблёного арахиса и сахара. Тесто выпекается в круглой чугунной форме. Края получаются тонкими и хрустящими. Середина, толстая и мягкая. Начинка, тёплая и сладкая. Ищите лоток с самой длинной очередью. Это он и есть.

## Ночные заведения с уличной едой

**Jalan Alor, Куала-Лумпур**, самая знаменитая ночная улица еды в городе. Она работает примерно с 5 вечера до 2 часов ночи. По вечерам улица закрыта для транспорта. Лотки уличной еды выстроены в ряд с обеих сторон, а в центре расположены открытые посадочные места. Еда здесь больше китайская, чем малайская: рыба на гриле, морепродукты, сатай и блюда из лапши. Атмосфера шумная, пропитанная дымом, и энергичная. Jalan Alor, туристическое место, но качество еды по-прежнему высокое, потому что конкуренция здесь жёсткая.

**Тэ тарик**, стандартный напиток в мамак-заведениях в любое время суток. Чай с молоком, приготовленный методом переливания, сладкий и сливочный. Его подают в стакане, а пенка сверху, признак правильно приготовленного напитка.

## Итог

Гастротуры Simply Enak в Малайзии включают вечерние сессии в хоукер-центрах и на pasar malam, где ночная гастрономическая сцена наиболее яркая. Местный гид, который знает продавцов и расписание, поможет вам больше поесть и меньше ходить.

title: What Happens in KL After the Sun Goes Down
excerpt: KL After Dark: Night Food Guide When the sun goes down in Kuala Lumpur, the streets change.

children.text: KL After Dark: Night Food Guide

When the sun goes down in Kuala Lumpur, the streets change. The traffic thins, the heat lifts, and the hawker stalls that were shuttered all afternoon roll out their woks and light their charcoal fires. KL after dark is not a club scene for most locals. It is a food scene. Families come out at 8 PM to eat. Office workers stop at pasar malams on their way home. Friends gather at tables set up on the roadside. The city eats well at night, and the best food is sold from mobile carts and plastic tables.
This guide covers three night food destinations in and around KL. Each has a different character. One is famous. One is local. One is massive.
Jalan Alor: The Famous Night Food Street

Jalan Alor is KL's most famous food street, and its reputation is earned. By 6 PM every evening, the road is closed to traffic. Hawker stalls line both sides. Plastic tables and chairs fill the street. The red glow of charcoal fires and string lights illuminates the whole strip.

The evening session at Jalan Alor starts at 6 PM and runs past midnight. The dinner rush is between 7 PM and 9 PM. The late-night crowd arrives after 10 PM, when the drinking crowd from nearby Changkat Bukit Bintang wanders over for supper.

**BBQ seafood** is the main event at Jalan Alor after dark. Stalls display fresh fish, prawns, squid, and stingray on ice beds. You pick what you want, the vendor weighs it, and it goes on the charcoal grill. The stingray (ikan bakar) is the standout :  slathered in sambal, wrapped in banana leaf, and grilled until the meat flakes apart. The sambal at the stalls near the Changkat end of the street is the spiciest. The sambal at the Pudu end is sweeter. Try both.

**Char kway teow** is essential eating on Jalan Alor at night. The stalls here cook over charcoal, which gives the noodles a smoky flavour that gas burners cannot produce. The best char kway teow on the street comes from the stall with the longest queue, which is usually the one near the middle of the strip. The queue moves fast. RM 8.

**Satay** at Jalan Alor is grilled over a long, narrow charcoal grill. The skewers are turned constantly. The fat from the meat drips onto the charcoal, creating bursts of smoke that flavour the meat. The peanut sauce is served warm. The ketupat (compressed rice cakes) come in small palm-leaf parcels.

**Wong Ah Wah** is the most famous restaurant on Jalan Alor, known for its grilled chicken wings. The wings are marinated in honey and soy, grilled over charcoal, and served with a sweet chilli dip. The skin is caramelised and slightly charred. The meat is moist. Order a plate of wings and a bottle of Sarsi.

**Dessert at Jalan Alor** is durian. Several stalls along the street sell durian by the table. The vendor opens the fruit in front of you and serves the segments on a plastic plate. Musang King (Mao Shan Wang) is the high-end variety :  creamy, bittersweet, with a smooth texture. It costs around RM 30-50 per fruit depending on the season. The kampung (village) durian is cheaper and has a more watery texture but is still worth trying.
SS2 Night Market: Petaling Jaya's Food Destination

SS2 is a neighbourhood in Petaling Jaya, the satellite city west of KL. Its night market (pasar malam) operates every Wednesday evening along the main road of SS2. It is a large market with hundreds of stalls, but the food section is the draw.
The market starts setting up around 4 PM and is fully operational by 6 PM. The food stalls are concentrated in the first section of the market. The produce and clothing stalls fill the rest.

**Apam balik** at SS2 is made on a large round griddle with multiple wells. The batter is poured in, the filling of sweet corn and crushed peanuts is scattered across it, and the pancake is folded in half. The version here has a thinner, crispier shell than the standard. RM 2.50.

**Lok lok** in SS2 operates from a converted van. Skewers of fish balls, sausages, tofu, squid, and vegetables are displayed in a refrigerated case. You pick your skewers and the vendor boils or deep-fries them. The dipping sauce is a communal bowl of sweet-spicy chilli sauce at your table. It is cheap, interactive, and the late-night crowd loves it. RM 1.50 per skewer.

**Grilled fish** at SS2 comes from a stall that sets up a full charcoal grill station. Whole fish :  usually ikan kembung (mackerel), ikan siakap (barramundi), or ikan pari (stingray) :  are stuffed with sambal, wrapped in banana leaf, and grilled. The process takes about 15 minutes. The vendor will tell you when it is ready and call your name. RM 10-15 for a whole fish.

**Cendol** at SS2 is made with coconut milk that the vendor extracts from fresh coconut on site. You can see the machine. The gula melaka is sourced from a supplier in Negeri Sembilan. The ice is shaved fine. RM 3.

**Fried banana** (pisang goreng) is sold at several stalls. The bananas are coated in a batter of rice flour and turmeric, then deep-fried until the outside is crisp and the inside is molten. The best version is at the stall next to the 7-Eleven. The batter is thinner and the bananas are ripened to the point of browning. RM 2 for five pieces.
Taman Connaught Night Market: The Longest in KL

Taman Connaught is a residential neighbourhood in Cheras, east of KL. Every Monday evening, the main road transforms into what is often called the longest night market in Malaysia. Over a thousand stalls stretch for over two kilometres. It is a spectacle.

The food section is in the first 500 metres. After that, the market shifts to clothes, household goods, electronics, and plants. The food stalls at the front are the busiest. The food stalls deeper in the market are where you find the surprises.

**BBQ seafood at Taman Connaught** is more varied than Jalan Alor. The stalls here serve grilled squid (sotong bakar), grilled prawns (udang bakar), and grilled fish in banana leaf (ikan bakar). The squid is the best option :  tender, smoky, and served with a chilli dip. RM 8 for a large squid.

**Roti john** is a Taman Connaught specialty. A split baguette filled with minced meat and egg, toasted on a flat grill, and served with chilli sauce and mayonnaise. The bread absorbs the egg and crisps up on the outside. The version here uses a 50-50 mix of beef mince and mutton mince.

**Keropok lekor** is a Malay fish sausage from Terengganu. It is deep-fried and served with a sweet-spicy chilli dip. The version at Taman Connaught comes from a vendor who drives down from Terengganu every Monday. The fish content is high enough that you can taste the mackerel. RM 3 for 10 pieces.

**Durian** at Taman Connaught is sold from pickup trucks loaded with fruit. The vendors are direct from the durian farms in Pahang. The price is lower than KL city centre. A Musang King here costs RM 25-35 per fruit, compared to RM 50 at Jalan Alor. The vendors open the fruit for you to inspect before you buy.

**Cendol** at Taman Connaught is made with ice shaved by a hand-cranked machine. The vendor has been at this same spot every Monday for 18 years. The coconut milk is fresh. The gula melaka is dark and slightly bitter. RM 3.
Practical Night Eating Tips for KL
Night markets in KL operate on set schedules. Taman Connaught is Monday only. SS2 is Wednesday only. Jalan Alor runs every night. Check the day before you plan to visit a pasar malam.
Cash is essential. Street vendors at night markets do not accept cards. Bring RM 50-100 in small notes for a proper eating session.
The best time to arrive at a night market is between 6:30 PM and 7:30 PM. The food is freshly cooked, the crowds have not peaked yet, and the best stalls still have stock.
Carry insect repellent. Night markets are outdoors and mosquitoes are active after dark.

Sit where you are told to sit. At busy stalls, the vendor directs you to a specific table. This is how they manage their service system. The table you are assigned may be shared with strangers. That is part of the experience.

KL's night food scene is vast. A guided evening tour makes it manageable. The Simply Enak KL night food tour covers Jalan Alor and whichever pasar malam is running that evening, with a local guide who knows the vendors and can navigate the crowds.

**Wong Ah Wah** ialah restoran paling terkenal di Jalan Alor, dikenali kerana kepak ayam panggangnya. Kepak diperap dengan madu dan kicap, dipanggang di atas arang, dan dihidangkan dengan celup cili manis. Kulitnya berkaramel dan sedikit hangus. Dagingnya lembap. Pesan sebungkus kepak dan sebotol Sarsi.

**Apam balik** di SS2 dibuat di atas kuali bulat yang besar dengan beberapa lubang. Adunan dituang ke dalam, inti jagung manis dan kacang tanah yang dihancurkan ditabur di atasnya, dan penkek dilipat dua. Versi di sini mempunyai kulit yang lebih nipis dan lebih rangup daripada yang biasa. RM 2.50.

## Pasar Malam Taman Connaught: Yang Terpanjang di KL

**Keropok lekor** adalah sosej ikan Melayu dari Terengganu. Ia digoreng dan disajikan dengan celup cili manis-pedas. Versi di Taman Connaught datang daripada seorang penjual yang memandu dari Terengganu setiap Isnin. Kandungan ikannya cukup tinggi sehingga anda boleh merasai ikan kembung. RM 3 untuk 10 keping.

Duduk di tempat yang diarahkan untuk duduk. Di gerai yang sibuk, penjual akan mengarahkan anda ke meja tertentu. Beginilah cara mereka mengurus sistem perkhidmatan mereka. Meja yang diberikan kepada anda mungkin dikongsi dengan orang yang tidak dikenali. Itulah sebahagian daripada pengalaman.

Scene makanan malam di KL adalah luas. Lawatan petang berpandu menjadikannya lebih terurus. Lawatan makanan malam Simply Enak KL merangkumi Jalan Alor dan mana-mana pasar malam yang berlangsung pada petang itu, dengan pemandu tempatan yang mengenali para penjual dan boleh mengharungi orang ramai.
translations.meta_title: KL Selepas Gelap: Panduan Makan Malam
translations.meta_description: Bila matahari terbenam di Kuala Lumpur, jalan-jalan berubah. Trafik berkurang, bahang surut, dan gerai-gerai penjaja yang ditutup sepanjang petang mula mengeluarkan kuali dan menyalakan api arang.

translations.title: KL After Dark：吉隆坡深夜美食攻略
translations.excerpt: 夜幕降临，吉隆坡的街道换了副模样。车流渐稀，暑气渐退，那些整个下午都门窗紧闭的小吃摊，一架起炒锅，点燃炭火。
translations.meta_title: 吉隆坡天黑后：夜间美食指南
translations.meta_description: 当太阳落山时，吉隆坡的街道就会发生变化。车流稀少，气温升高，整个下午都关着门的小贩摊位纷纷推出炒锅，点燃炭火。
translations.content_markdown:
茨厂街的晚间营业从傍晚六点开始，一直持续到午夜之后。晚餐高峰在晚上七点到九点之间。晚上十点过后则是宵夜时段，这时附近武吉免登区（Changkat Bukit Bintang）喝完酒的人群会陆续过来吃夜宵。

**旺阿華**是阿罗街最著名的餐厅，以烤鸡翅闻名。鸡翅用蜂蜜和酱油腌制后，以炭火烤制，搭配甜辣酱上桌。鸡皮焦糖化并略带焦香，肉质鲜嫩多汁。点一盘鸡翅，再来一瓶沙士汽水。

SS2 的 **Apam balik（曼煎饼）** 是在一个带有多个圆形凹槽的大铁板上制作的。将面糊倒入，撒上甜玉米和碎花生的馅料，再把饼对折。这里售卖的版本外壳比一般的更薄、更脆。售价 2.50 林吉特。

## 蒂曼康纳夜市：吉隆坡最长的夜市

**Keropok lekor** 是来自登嘉楼的一种马来鱼饼。它经过油炸，配上甜辣酱一起吃。Taman Connaught 的版本来自一位每周一专程从登嘉楼驱车而来的摊主。鱼肉含量很高，可以吃出鲭鱼的味道。10 条只要 3 林吉。

商家让你坐哪里就坐哪里。在繁忙的摊位，商家会指引你到特定的桌子。这是他们管理服务的方式。分配给你的桌子可能需要与陌生人共用。这是体验的一部分。

吉隆坡的夜市美食版图十分广阔。跟着导游的夜间美食之旅能让这一切变得轻松易行。Simply Enak 吉隆坡夜间美食之旅涵盖阿罗街以及当晚开放营业的夜市，由熟悉各家摊主、能在人群中自如穿行的当地导游带领。

translations.title: KL After Dark: Streetfood-Guide für die Nacht
translations.excerpt: Wenn in Kuala Lumpur die Sonne untergeht, verwandeln sich die Straßen. Der Verkehr lässt nach, die Hitze weicht, und die Garküchen, die den ganzen Nachmittag geschlossen hatten, holen ihre Woks hervor und entzünden die Holzkohle.
translations.meta_title: KL After Dark: Night Food Guide
translations.meta_description: Wenn in Kuala Lumpur die Sonne untergeht, verändern sich die Straßen. Der Verkehr lässt nach, die Hitze steigt, und die Straßenhändler, die den ganzen Nachmittag über geschlossen waren, rollen ihre Woks aus und zünden ihr Holzkohlefeuer an
translations.content_markdown:
Die Abendschicht auf Jalan Alor beginnt um 18 Uhr und dauert bis nach Mitternacht. Der Ansturm zum Abendessen ist zwischen 19 und 21 Uhr. Das späte Publikum kommt nach 22 Uhr, wenn die trinkfreudige Menge aus dem nahegelegenen Changkat Bukit Bintang zum späten Abendessen herüberkommt.

**Wong Ah Wah** ist das berühmteste Restaurant auf der Jalan Alor, bekannt für seine gegrillten Hähnchenflügel. Die Flügel werden in Honig und Sojasauce mariniert, über Holzkohle gegrillt und mit einem süßen Chilidip serviert. Die Haut ist karamellisiert und leicht angekohlt. Das Fleisch ist saftig. Bestelle eine Platte Flügel und eine Flasche Sarsi.

**Apam balik** an SS2 wird auf einer großen runden Grillplatte mit mehreren Mulden zubereitet. Der Teig wird hineingegossen, die Füllung aus süßem Mais und zerdrückten Erdnüssen darüber gestreut, und der Pfannkuchen wird in der Mitte gefaltet. Die Version hier hat eine dünnere, knusprigere Schale als die Standardversion. RM 2,50.

## Taman Connaught Nachtmarkt: Der Längste in KL

**Keropok lekor** ist eine malaiische Fischwurst aus Terengganu. Sie wird frittiert und mit einem süß-scharfen Chilli-Dip serviert. Die Version in Taman Connaught kommt von einem Anbieter, der jeden Montag aus Terengganu herunterfährt. Der Fischanteil ist hoch genug, dass man die Makrele herausschmecken kann. RM 3 für 10 Stück.

Setzen Sie sich dorthin, wo Sie hingesetzt werden. An belebten Ständen weist Sie der Verkäufer einem bestimmten Tisch zu. So verwalten sie ihr Servicesystem. Der Ihnen zugewiesene Tisch kann mit Fremden geteilt werden. Das gehört zum Erlebnis dazu.

Die nächtliche Food-Szene in KL ist riesig. Eine geführte Abendtour macht sie überschaubar. Die Simply Enak KL Night Food Tour deckt Jalan Alor und den Pasar Malam ab, der an dem jeweiligen Abend stattfindet, mit einem lokalen Guide, der die Verkäufer kennt und sich durch die Menschenmassen navigieren kann.

translations.title: KL After Dark: Guía gastronómica nocturna
translations.excerpt: Al caer el sol en Kuala Lumpur, las calles se transforman. El tráfico se aligera, el calor cede, y los puestos callejeros que estuvieron cerrados toda la tarde sacan sus woks y encienden el fuego de carbón.
translations.meta_title: KL After Dark: Guía de comida nocturna
translations.meta_description: Cuando se pone el sol en Kuala Lumpur, las calles cambian. El tráfico disminuye, el calor disminuye y los puestos de vendedores ambulantes que estuvieron cerrados toda la tarde sacan sus woks y encienden su fuego de carbón.
translations.content_markdown:
La sesión nocturna en Jalan Alor comienza a las 6 PM y se extiende pasada la medianoche. La hora punta de la cena es entre las 7 PM y las 9 PM. La multitud nocturna llega después de las 10 PM, cuando la gente que ha estado bebiendo en el cercano Changkat Bukit Bintang viene a buscar una cena tardía.

**Wong Ah Wah** es el restaurante más famoso de Jalan Alor, conocido por sus alitas de pollo a la parrilla. Las alitas se marinan en miel y salsa de soja, se asan al carbón y se sirven con una salsa de chile dulce. La piel está caramelizada y ligeramente chamuscada. La carne está jugosa. Pide un plato de alitas y una botella de Sarsi.

El **Apam balik** en SS2 se hace en una plancha redonda grande con múltiples cavidades. Se vierte la masa, el relleno de maíz dulce y maní triturado se esparce sobre ella, y el panqueque se dobla por la mitad. La versión de aquí tiene una capa más fina y crujiente que la estándar. RM 2.50.

## Mercado Nocturno de Taman Connaught: El Más Largo de KL

**El keropok lekor** es una salchicha de pescado malaya de Terengganu. Se fríe y se sirve con una salsa de chile agridulce. La versión de Taman Connaught proviene de un vendedor que viaja desde Terengganu cada lunes. El contenido de pescado es lo suficientemente alto como para poder saborear la caballa. 3 RM por 10 piezas.

Siéntate donde te indiquen que te sientes. En los puestos concurridos, el vendedor te dirige a una mesa específica. Así es como manejan su sistema de servicio. La mesa que te asignen puede ser compartida con desconocidos. Eso es parte de la experiencia.

La escena gastronómica nocturna de KL es amplia. Un tour nocturno guiado la hace manejable. El tour gastronómico nocturno Simply Enak KL cubre Jalan Alor y cualquier pasar malam que esté funcionando esa noche, con un guía local que conoce a los vendedores y puede manejar las multitudes.

translations.title: KL After Dark : Guide des saveurs nocturnes
translations.excerpt: Quand le soleil se couche à Kuala Lumpur, les rues se transforment. La circulation s'apaise, la chaleur retombe, et les hawkers, restés muets tout l'après-midi, sortent leurs woks et ravivent la braise.
translations.meta_title: KL After Dark : Guide alimentaire de nuit
translations.meta_description: Lorsque le soleil se couche à Kuala Lumpur, les rues changent. La circulation s'amenuise, la chaleur monte et les échoppes de vendeurs ambulants, fermées tout l'après-midi, sortent leurs woks et allument leur feu de charbon de bois.
translations.content_markdown:
La session du soir à Jalan Alor commence à 18h et se prolonge après minuit. L'affluence du dîner se situe entre 19h et 21h. La foule tardive arrive après 22h, quand les buveurs du Changkat Bukit Bintang voisin viennent prendre un souper.

**Wong Ah Wah** est le restaurant le plus célèbre de Jalan Alor, connu pour ses ailes de poulet grillées. Les ailes sont marinées dans du miel et de la sauce soja, grillées au charbon de bois, et servies avec une sauce au piment sucrée. La peau est caramélisée et légèrement carbonisée. La viande est moelleuse. Commandez une assiette d'ailes et une bouteille de Sarsi.

L'**apam balik** de SS2 est préparé sur une grande plaque ronde avec plusieurs alvéoles. La pâte y est versée, la garniture de maïs sucré et de cacahuètes concassées est éparpillée dessus, et la crêpe est pliée en deux. La version proposée ici a une coque plus fine et plus croustillante que la version standard. 2,50 RM.

## Marché de nuit de Taman Connaught : Le plus long de KL

Le **keropok lekor** est une saucisse de poisson malaisienne originaire de Terengganu. Elle est frite et servie avec une sauce pimentée sucrée-épicée. La version à Taman Connaught provient d'un vendeur qui descend de Terengganu chaque lundi. La teneur en poisson est suffisamment élevée pour que l'on puisse goûter le maquereau. RM 3 pour 10 pièces.

Asseyez-vous là où l'on vous dit de vous asseoir. Dans les stands très fréquentés, le vendeur vous dirige vers une table précise. C'est ainsi qu'ils gèrent leur système de service. La table qui vous est attribuée peut être partagée avec des inconnus. Cela fait partie de l'expérience.

La scène gastronomique nocturne de KL est vaste. Une visite guidée en soirée la rend plus gérable. Le circuit gastronomique nocturne Simply Enak KL couvre Jalan Alor et le pasar malam qui a lieu ce soir-là, avec un guide local qui connaît les vendeurs et sait naviguer dans la foule.

translations.title: KL After Dark: Nachtvoedselgids
translations.excerpt: Als de zon ondergaat in Kuala Lumpur veranderen de straten. Het verkeer neemt af, de hitte neemt toe en de kraampjes met luiken die de hele middag gesloten waren, rollen hun wok uit en steken hun houtskoolvuur aan
translations.meta_title: KL After Dark: Nachtvoedselgids
translations.meta_description: Als de zon ondergaat in Kuala Lumpur veranderen de straten. Het verkeer neemt af, de hitte neemt toe en de kraampjes met luiken die de hele middag gesloten waren, rollen hun wok uit en steken hun houtskoolvuur aan
translations.content_markdown:
De avondsessie op Jalan Alor begint om 18.00 uur en duurt tot na middernacht. De dinerdrukte is tussen 19.00 en 21.00 uur. Het laatnachtelijke publiek komt na 22.00 uur, wanneer het drinkende publiek van het nabijgelegen Changkat Bukit Bintang komt wandelen voor een late hap.

**Wong Ah Wah** is het beroemdste restaurant op Jalan Alor, bekend om zijn gegrilde kippenvleugels. De vleugels worden gemarineerd in honing en soja, gegrild boven houtskool, en geserveerd met een zoete chilidip. Het vel is gekarameliseerd en licht geschroeid. Het vlees is sappig. Bestel een bord vleugels en een fles Sarsi.

**Apam balik** bij SS2 wordt gemaakt op een grote ronde bakplaat met meerdere holtes. Het beslag wordt erin gegoten, de vulling van zoete maïs en gemalen pinda's wordt erover gestrooid, en de pannenkoek wordt dubbelgevouwen. De versie hier heeft een dunnere, knapperigere korst dan de standaard. RM 2,50.

## Taman Connaught Nachtmarkt: De Langste in KL

**Keropok lekor** is een Maleisische visworst uit Terengganu. Hij wordt gefrituurd en geserveerd met een zoet-pittige chilidip. De versie bij Taman Connaught komt van een verkoper die elke maandag vanuit Terengganu naar beneden rijdt. Het visgehalte is hoog genoeg dat je de makreel kunt proeven. RM 3 voor 10 stuks.

Ga zitten waar je wordt verteld te zitten. Bij drukke kraampjes wijst de verkoper je een specifieke tafel aan. Zo beheren ze hun servicesysteem. De tafel die je krijgt toegewezen, kan gedeeld worden met vreemden. Dat hoort bij de ervaring.

De nachtelijke eetcultuur van KL is enorm. Een begeleide avondtour maakt het behapbaar. De Simply Enak KL-nachtfoodtour omvat Jalan Alor en de pasar malam die die avond plaatsvindt, met een lokale gids die de kraamhouders kent en door de drukte kan navigeren.
translations.content: Er is geen tekst om te vertalen. Het object is leeg. Geef de Engelse tekst die je vertaald wilt hebben naar het Nederlands.

translations.title: KL After Dark: гид по ночной еде
translations.excerpt: Когда солнце садится в Куала-Лумпуре, улицы меняются. Движение транспорта становится реже, тепловые лифты и ларьки с ставнями, которые весь день были закрыты ставнями, выкатывают воки и разжигают древесный уголь.
translations.meta_title: KL After Dark: гид по ночной еде
translations.meta_description: Когда солнце садится в Куала-Лумпуре, улицы меняются. Движение транспорта становится реже, тепловые лифты и ларьки с ставнями, которые весь день были закрыты ставнями, выкатывают воки и разжигают древесный уголь.
translations.content_markdown:
Вечерняя сессия на Джалан Ало́р начинается в 6 вечера и продолжается за полночь. Пик ужина приходится на период с 7 до 9 вечера. Поздняя публика приходит после 10 вечера, когда пьющие из соседнего Чангкат Букит Бинтанг заглядывают сюда на поздний ужин.

**Wong Ah Wah**, самый знаменитый ресторан на Джалан Алор, известный своими куриными крылышками на гриле. Крылышки маринуют в мёде и соевом соусе, жарят на углях и подают со сладким чили-соусом. Кожица карамелизированная и слегка обугленная. Мясо сочное. Закажите тарелку крылышек и бутылку Sarsi.

**Апам балик** в SS2 готовится на большой круглой сковороде с несколькими углублениями. Тесто наливается, начинка из сладкой кукурузы и дроблёного арахиса рассыпается сверху, а блин складывается пополам. Здесь он более тонкий и хрустящий по сравнению со стандартным. 2,50 ринггита.

## Ночной рынок Таман-Коннот: самый длинный в Куала-Лумпуре

**Keropok lekor**, малайская рыбная колбаса из Теренггану. Обжаривается во фритюре и подаётся со сладко-острым соусом чили. Версия в Taman Connaught, от продавца, который приезжает из Теренггану каждый понедельник. Содержание рыбы достаточно высокое, чтобы чувствовалась скумбрия. RM 3 за 10 штук.

Садитесь туда, куда вам скажут сесть. На популярных прилавках продавец указывает вам конкретный столик. Так устроена их система обслуживания. Назначенный вам столик может оказаться общим с незнакомцами. Это часть опыта.

Ночная гастрономическая сцена Куала-Лумпура огромна. Вечерняя экскурсия с гидом делает её вполне доступной. Ночной гастрономический тур Simply Enak KL охватывает Джалан Алор и тот ночной рынок (pasar malam), который работает в этот вечер, в сопровождении местного гида, знающего продавцов и умеющего ориентироваться в толпе.

translations.excerpt: クアラルンプールは日が沈むと街並みが変わります。交通量が減り、暑さが和らぎ、午後中ずっとシャッターが閉まっていた行商の屋台が中華鍋を出して炭火に火をつける
translations.meta_title: KLアフターダーク：夜のグルメガイド

translations.content_markdown:
ジャラン・アロールの夜の部は午後6時に始まり、深夜を過ぎても続く。夕食のラッシュは午後7時から9時の間。深夜の客層は午後10時以降にやって来る。近くのチャンカット・ブキッ・ビンタンの飲んだ後のグループが夜食に流れてくるのだ。

**ウォン・アー・ワー**は、Jalan Alor で最も有名なレストランで、グリルした手羽先で知られています。手羽先は蜂蜜と醤油にマリネされ、炭火で焼かれ、甘辛いチリソースを添えて出されます。皮はキャラメル状に焼かれ、軽く焦げ目がついています。肉はジューシーです。手羽先を一皿と、サルシのボトルを1本注文しましょう。

SS2の**アパンバラク**は複数のくぼみがある大きな丸い鉄板で作られる。生地が流し込まれ、甘いトウモロコシと砕いたピーナッツのフィリングが散らされ、パンケーキが半分に折りたたまれる。这里的版本外殼更薄、更脆，比標準的更勝一籌。RM 2.50。

## タマン・コーナート夜市：KLで最長

**ケロポッレコル**は、トレンガヌ州原産のマレー風の魚ソーセージです。揚げて、甘辛いチリソースを添えて提供されます。タマン・コノートで売られているものは、毎週月曜日にトレンガヌから車でやって来る業者から仕入れたものです。魚の含有量が高いため、サバの味がしっかり感じられます。10本入りでRM 3です。

指示された席に座りましょう。混雑している屋台では、店主が特定のテーブルに案内してくれます。これは彼らのサービスシステムの管理方法です。割り当てられたテーブルは、見知らぬ他人と相席になることもあります。それも経験の一部です。

クアラルンプール（KL）の夜の食事情は広大です。ガイド付きの夜のツアーなら、無理なく楽しむことができます。Simply Enak KL 夜のフードツアーでは、その夜に開催されているパサール・マラムと Jalan Alor（ジャラン・アロー）を巡り、屋台を知り尽くした地元ガイドが人混みをうまく案内してくれます。

translations.content_markdown:
A sessão noturna na Jalan Alor começa às 18h e vai até depois da meia-noite. O rush do jantar acontece entre 19h e 21h. A multidão noturna chega depois das 22h, quando o público que estava bebendo nas proximidades do Changkat Bukit Bintang vem para a ceia.

**Wong Ah Wah** é o restaurante mais famoso de Jalan Alor, conhecido por suas asas de frango grelhadas. As asas são marinadas em mel e molho de soja, grelhadas no carvão e servidas com um molho de pimenta doce. A pele é caramelizada e levemente chamuscada. A carne está suculenta. Peça um prato de asas e uma garrafa de Sarsi.

A **apam balik** em SS2 é feita numa frigideira redonda grande com vários compartimentos. A massa é vertida, o recheio de milho doce e amendoim triturado é espalhado por cima, e a panqueca é dobrada ao meio. A versão daqui tem uma casca mais fina e mais crocante do que a tradicional. RM 2.50.

## Mercado Noturno de Taman Connaught: O Maior de KL

**Keropok lekor** é uma salsicha malaia de peixe de Terengganu. É frita e servida com um molho de pimenta agridoce. A versão em Taman Connaught vem de um vendedor que viaja de Terengganu todas as segundas-feiras. O teor de peixe é suficientemente alto para se sentir o sabor da cavala. RM 3 por 10 unidades.

Sente-se onde lhe disserem para se sentar. Em barracas movimentadas, o vendedor indica-lhe uma mesa específica. É assim que eles gerem o seu sistema de serviço. A mesa que lhe for atribuída pode ser partilhada com estranhos. Isso faz parte da experiência.

A cena gastronômica noturna de KL é vasta. Um passeio noturno guiado torna isso administrável. O Simply Enak KL night food tour cobre a Jalan Alor e qualquer *pasar malam* que esteja funcionando naquela noite, com um guia local que conhece os vendedores e consegue navegar pelas multidões.

title: Penang Markets Worth Waking Up Early For
excerpt: A Local's Guide to Penang's Markets Penang's markets are older than the state itself in some cases.

children.text: A Local's Guide to Penang's Markets

Penang's markets are older than the state itself in some cases. Chowrasta Market has been operating since the 1890s. Air Itam market has been feeding the hillside communities for over a century. The night markets at Batu Ferringhi are newer, but the stallholders bring the same family recipes that have been passed down through generations.

Shopping at a Penang market is a different experience from the KL equivalent. The island's markets are smaller, more concentrated, and the food is more specific to Penang's particular mix of Malay, Chinese, Nyonya, and Indian cultures. This guide covers the four essential markets and what to eat at each.
Chowrasta Market: George Town's Market Heart

Chowrasta Market sits at the intersection of Penang Road and Lebuh Tamil, a five-minute walk from the Komtar transport hub. It has been the main market of George Town since the British colonial era. The building is a 1970s concrete structure, but the market has occupied this site for over 130 years.

The ground floor is a wet market with fresh produce, meat, and seafood. The vendors here supply most of the restaurants in George Town. The fruit section is the best in the city for tropical fruit :  durian, mangosteen, cempedak, and the tiny sweet bananas (pisang emas) that Penang is known for.
The upper floor and the surrounding streets are where the food action is. This is where you find the market food that Penangites have been eating for generations.

**Pasembur** is a Penang-specific salad of shredded cucumber, turnip, bean sprouts, prawn fritters, and tofu, served with a thick sweet potato and chilli sauce. The sauce is the defining element :  it is sweet, spicy, and slightly nutty, nothing like the peanut sauce used in rojak. The pasembur stall at the entrance to the upper floor of Chowrasta has been run by the same family since the 1950s. The current owner is the granddaughter of the original vendor. She makes the sauce fresh each morning. RM 5 for a regular portion.

**Rojak** in Penang is made with a darker, thicker shrimp paste sauce than the KL version. Local fruits :  unripe mango, jambu air (wax apple), papaya, pineapple :  are mixed with cucumber and turnip, tossed in the sauce, and topped with crushed peanuts and toasted sesame seeds. The rojak stall near the Penang Road entrance has a queue that snakes around the corner by lunchtime. The secret is the belacan :  the owner sources it from a specific supplier in Balik Pulau and toasts it himself before grinding it into the sauce.

**Asam laksa** at Chowrasta is served by a stall on the lower level that has no name and no sign. You find it by following the smell of tamarind and fish broth. The owner starts cooking at 8 AM and is usually sold out by 1 PM. The broth is thick, intensely sour, and packed with shredded mackerel. It is the real deal, and it costs RM 4.50.

**Nutmeg** is a Penang specialty. Chowrasta Market has several stalls selling preserved nutmeg strips, nutmeg juice (air buah pala), and nutmeg pickles. The preserved nutmeg is sweet and chewy, served as a snack or added to drinks. The nutmeg juice is a refreshing, slightly floral drink that is believed to aid digestion. Try a glass at the stall opposite the fish section.
Pulau Tikus Market: Where George Town's Old Families Shop

Pulau Tikus is an older, wealthier neighbourhood in George Town, and its market reflects that. The building is cleaner than Chowrasta, the aisles are wider, and the produce is more carefully curated. This is where George Town's Nyonya families and expatriates do their shopping.
The food section at Pulau Tikus is small but high quality. Two stalls stand out.

**Nasi kandar** is the dish to order here. Rice served with a selection of curries and sides that you point at from the display. The vendor pours the curry sauce over the rice from a height :  a technique called "banjir" (flooding) that mixes the flavours as the sauce lands. The nasi kandar stall at Pulau Tikus has been operating for over thirty years. The fried chicken is cooked in a turmeric batter that stays crispy even after the curry sauce hits it. The okra is stir-fried with dried shrimp. The fish curry uses a sour tamarind base that balances the richness of the coconut milk curries. RM 7 for a full plate.

**Mee goreng** at the Indian-Muslim stall at the front of the market is a Penang version of the dish :  yellower noodles, more tomato sauce in the seasoning, and a spicier finish than the KL version. It is served with a wedge of lime and a side of pickled chillies.

**Kuih** at Pulau Tikus Market is made by a Nyonya vendor who supplies several restaurants in George Town. Her kuih lapis (layered rice flour cake) has 12 distinct layers, each steamed one at a time. Her ondeh-ondeh (palm sugar balls in grated coconut) are made fresh at 7 AM and sell out by 9 AM. RM 1 per piece.
Air Itam Market: The Hillside Market

Air Itam Market sits at the foot of the hill leading up to Kek Lok Si temple. It is a smaller market than Chowrasta or Pulau Tikus, serving the residential community of Air Itam rather than the whole island. The food here is less polished and more rewarding.

**Penang laksa** at the Air Itam market is the version that locals argue about. The broth uses more tamarind and less sugar than the George Town versions. The mackerel is shredded by hand, not blended. The noodles are cut wider. The herbs :  mint, torch ginger, daun kesum (Vietnamese mint) :  are piled on generously. The laksa stall at the back of the market has a handwritten sign and a queue that moves fast. RM 5.

**Hokkien char** is a Penang stir-fried noodle dish that is less famous than Hokkien mee but equally good. Thick yellow noodles are fried with dark soy sauce, pork belly, squid, and cabbage. The Penang version uses more pork lard than the KL version, giving the noodles a glossy sheen and a savoury depth. The Hokkien char stall at Air Itam market opens at 11 AM and closes when the pork belly runs out.

**Cincau** is grass jelly drink. The Air Itam version is made from scratch using the leaves of the mesona plant, not from powder. The jelly is darker, firmer, and has a herbal bitterness that the powdered version lacks. Served with shaved ice and evaporated milk. RM 2.
Batu Ferringhi Night Market: The Beach Bazaar

The Batu Ferringhi night market runs along the main beach road every evening from 7 PM. It is the most tourist-heavy market on this list, but it still serves food that Penangites drive across the island for.
The food section is at the eastern end of the market. The offerings lean towards Malay and Malay-Chinese street food, with a few Indian stalls mixed in.

**Ikan bakar** is the main event. Fresh fish, squid, and prawns displayed on ice. You pick what you want, and the vendor grills it over charcoal while you wait. The stingray (ikan pari) is the best option. It is slathered in sambal, wrapped in banana leaf, and grilled until the flesh is flaky. The sambal at the stall nearest the beach access point is made with fresh chilli, not chilli paste. You can taste the difference. RM 10 for a large piece.

**Satay** at Batu Ferringhi comes from a Malay vendor who has been at this market for twenty years. The skewers are marinated in turmeric and coconut milk, grilled over coconut charcoal, and served with a peanut sauce that has visible chunks of peanut. The ketupat (compressed rice cakes) that come with it are wrapped in palm leaves and made fresh.

**Apam balik** at the night market is made on a large cast-iron griddle. The vendor spreads the batter thin, sprinkles sweet corn and crushed peanuts across it, folds it, and cuts it into wedges. The edges are lacy and crisp. The centre is soft and sweet. RM 3.

**Cendol** from the Malay stall near the market midpoint uses fresh pandan jelly and coconut milk that the vendor extracts by hand. The gula melaka is sourced from a supplier in Balik Pulau who has been tapping the same palm trees for thirty years.
Practical Market Tips for Penang
Cash is required at every market on this list. No stall accepts cards. ATMs are available at the Komtar shopping centre near Chowrasta and at the 7-Eleven on Batu Ferringhi main road.

Chowrasta and Pulau Tikus are morning markets. Go between 7 AM and 10 AM for the best selection and the freshest food. Air Itam market is active from 8 AM to 2 PM. Batu Ferringhi is an evening market :  do not arrive before 6:30 PM.
The fruit at Chowrasta is cheaper than the supermarket, but check for ripeness. The vendors are honest about quality :  a good vendor will tell you if a fruit is not ready to eat.
If a stall has a queue, join it. Penangites know their market food. A queue at 8 AM at a market stall means the food is worth waiting for.

Markets can be overwhelming on a first visit. The Simply Enak Penang market tour visits Chowrasta and Pulau Tikus with a local guide who knows the history of each stall, the best things to order, and the vendors by name. It is the fastest way to go from overwhelmed to eating with confidence.

translations.excerpt: Pasaran Pulau Pinang lebih tua daripada negeri itu sendiri dalam beberapa kes. Pasar Chowrasta telah beroperasi sejak tahun 1890-an. Pasar Air Itam telah memberi makan kepada komuniti lereng bukit selama lebih satu abad. n
translations.content_markdown:
Tingkat bawah adalah pasar basah yang menjual hasil segar, daging, dan makanan laut. Penjual-penjual di sini membekalkan kebanyakan restoran di George Town. Bahagian buah-buahan adalah yang terbaik di bandar untuk buah-buahan tropika : durian, manggis, cempedak, dan pisang emas kecil yang manis yang menjadi terkenal dengan Pulau Pinang.

**Rojak** di Pulau Pinang disediakan dengan sos pasta udang yang lebih gelap dan lebih pekat berbanding versi KL. Buah-buahan tempatan : mangga muda, jambu air (jambu air), betik, nanas : dicampur dengan timun dan lobak, dibalut dengan sos, dan ditaburkan dengan kacang tanah yang dihancurkan serta bijan panggang. Gerai rojak berhampiran pintu masuk Jalan Penang mempunyai barisan yang berselerak sehingga ke penjuru pada waktu tengah hari. Rahsianya adalah belacan : pemiliknya mendapatkan bekalan daripada pembekal khusus di Balik Pulau dan memanggangnya sendiri sebelum mengisar menjadi sos.

Bahagian makanan di Pulau Tikus adalah kecil tetapi berkualiti tinggi. Dua gerai menonjol.

## Pasar Air Itam: Pasar di Lereng Bukit

## Pasar Malam Batu Ferringhi: Bazaar Pantai

**Apam balik** di pasar malam dibuat di atas kuali besi tuang yang besar. Penjual menyebarkan adunan secara nipis, menaburkan jagung manis dan kacang tanah yang dihancurkan ke seluruh permukaan, melipatnya, dan memotongnya menjadi baji. Bahagian tepinya berbentuk jala dan rangup. Bahagian tengahnya lembut dan manis. RM 3.

Pasar boleh menjadi pengalaman yang mengelirukan pada lawatan pertama. Lawatan pasar Simply Enak Penang melawat Chowrasta dan Pulau Tikus dengan pemandu tempatan yang mengetahui sejarah setiap gerai, hidangan terbaik untuk dipesan, dan nama para penjual. Ia adalah cara terpantas untuk berubah daripada keliru kepada makan dengan yakin.

translations.meta_description: 在某些情况下，槟城的市场比槟城本身还要古老。 Chowrasta 市场自 1890 年代以来一直营业。一个多世纪以来，亚依淡市场一直为山坡社区提供食物。然后
translations.content_markdown:
一楼是湿货市场，售卖新鲜农产品、肉类和海鲜。这里的供应商为乔治市的大部分餐厅供货。水果区是全城最好的热带水果采购地：榴莲、山竹、菠萝蜜，以及槟城闻名的小甜蕉（pisang emas）。

槟城版的 **Rojak（啰惹）** 使用的虾酱比吉隆坡版本颜色更深、质地更浓稠。当地水果,, 未成熟的芒果、水蓊（莲雾）、木瓜、菠萝,, 与黄瓜和芜菁混合，淋上酱汁拌匀，再撒上碎花生和烤芝麻。靠近 Penang Road 入口处的啰惹摊位，午餐时间前队伍会排到拐角处。秘诀就在于虾酱（belacan）：摊主专门从 Balik Pulau 的一家供应商处采购原料，并亲自烘烤后研磨成酱。

浮罗池滑的熟食区不大，但品质很高。其中有两个摊位尤为出色。

## Air Itam 市场：山坡上的市场

## 峇都丁宜夜市：海滨市集

夜市的**曼煎糕 (Apam balik)** 是在一个大铸铁煎盘上制作的。摊主把面糊摊薄，撒上甜玉米粒和碎花生，对折后切成楔形块。边缘酥脆，带着蕾丝般的花纹；中间松软香甜。3 林吉特。

第一次逛市场可能会感到不知所措。Simply Enak Penang市场导览由当地向导带领参观Chowrasta和丹绒道光市场，向导熟悉每个摊位的历史、最值得点的菜品，还能叫出摊主的名字。这是从不知所措到放心品尝美食的最快途径。

translations.title: Penangs Märkte: Ein Guide aus lokaler Sicht
translations.excerpt: Die Märkte von Penang sind zum Teil älter als der Bundesstaat selbst. Der Chowrasta-Markt öffnete bereits in den 1890er Jahren. Der Air Itam-Markt versorgt die Hügelgemeinden seit über einem Jahrhundert mit Lebensmitteln. Dann
translations.meta_title: Ein lokaler Führer zu den Märkten von Penang
translations.meta_description: Die Märkte von Penang sind teilweise älter als der Staat selbst. Der Chowrasta-Markt ist seit den 1890er Jahren in Betrieb. Der Air Itam-Markt versorgt die Berggemeinden seit über einem Jahrhundert mit Nahrung. Dann
translations.content_markdown:
Das Erdgeschoss ist ein Nassmarkt mit frischem Obst und Gemüse, Fleisch und Meeresfrüchten. Die Verkäufer hier beliefern die meisten Restaurants in George Town. Die Obstabteilung ist die beste der Stadt für tropische Früchte : Durian, Mangostane, Cempedak und die winzigen süßen Bananen (Pisang Emas), für die Penang bekannt ist.

**Rojak** in Penang wird mit einer dunkleren, dickeren Garnelenpastensoße zubereitet als die Version aus KL. Lokale Früchte : unreife Mango, Jambu Air (Wachsapfel), Papaya, Ananas : werden mit Gurke und Rübe vermischt, in der Soße geschwenkt und mit zerdrückten Erdnüssen und geröstetem Sesam garniert. Der Rojak-Stand in der Nähe des Eingangs der Penang Road hat zur Mittagszeit eine Schlange, die sich um die Ecke schlängelt. Das Geheimnis ist der Belacan : der Besitzer bezieht ihn von einem bestimmten Lieferanten in Balik Pulau und röstet ihn selbst, bevor er ihn zu Soße mahlt.

Die Lebensmittelabteilung bei Pulau Tikus ist klein, aber von hoher Qualität. Zwei Stände stechen hervor.

## Air Itam Market: Der Bergmarkt

## Batu Ferringhi Nachtmarkt: Der Strandbasar

**Apam balik** am Nachtmarkt wird auf einer großen gusseisernen Grillplatte zubereitet. Der Verkäufer verteilt den Teig dünn, streut süßen Mais und zerdrückte Erdnüsse darüber, klappt ihn zusammen und schneidet ihn in dreieckige Stücke. Die Ränder sind knusprig und kross. Die Mitte ist weich und süß. RM 3.

Märkte können beim ersten Besuch überwältigend sein. Die Simply Enak Penang Market Tour besucht Chowrasta und Pulau Tikus mit einem einheimischen Guide, der die Geschichte jedes Standes kennt, weiß, was man am besten bestellen sollte, und die Verkäufer mit Namen kennt. Es ist der schnellste Weg, von überwältigt zu selbstbewusstem Genießen zu gelangen.

## Mercado Nocturno de Batu Ferringhi: El Bazar de la Playa

translations.content_markdown:
Le rez-de-chaussée est un marché humide avec des produits frais, de la viande et des fruits de mer. Les vendeurs ici approvisionnent la plupart des restaurants de George Town. La section des fruits est la meilleure de la ville pour les fruits tropicaux : le durian, le mangoustan, le cempedak, et les petites bananes sucrées (pisang emas) pour lesquelles Penang est connue.

**Le Rojak** à Penang est préparé avec une sauce à base de pâte de crevettes plus foncée et plus épaisse que la version de KL. Les fruits locaux : mangue non mûre, jambu air (pomme-cire), papaye, ananas : sont mélangés avec du concombre et du navet, enrobés dans la sauce, puis parsemés de cacahuètes concassées et de graines de sésame grillées. L'étal de rojak près de l'entrée de Penang Road voit une file d'attente qui serpente au coin de la rue à l'heure du déjeuner. Le secret réside dans le belacan : le propriétaire se le procure auprès d'un fournisseur spécifique à Balik Pulau et le fait griller lui-même avant de le moudre pour en faire la sauce.

La section alimentaire de Pulau Tikus est petite mais de grande qualité. Deux stands se distinguent.

## Marché d'Air Itam : Le marché à flanc de colline

## Marché de nuit de Batu Ferringhi : Le bazar de la plage

L'**apam balik** du marché nocturne est préparé sur une grande plaque en fonte. Le vendeur étale finement la pâte, saupoudre de maïs sucré et de cacahuètes concassées, la plie et la découpe en parts. Les bords sont dentelés et croustillants. Le centre est moelleux et sucré. 3 RM.

translations.excerpt: Рынки Пенанга в некоторых случаях старше самого штата. Рынок Чораста работает с 1890-х годов. Рынок Эйр-Итам кормит жителей склонов холмов уже более века. Затем
translations.meta_title: Местный путеводитель по рынкам Пенанга
translations.meta_description: Рынки Пенанга в некоторых случаях старше самого штата. Рынок Чораста работает с 1890-х годов. Рынок Эйр-Итам кормит жителей склонов холмов уже более века. Затем
translations.content_markdown:
Первый этаж, это мокрый рынок со свежими продуктами, мясом и морепродуктами. Торговцы здесь снабжают большинство ресторанов Джорджтауна. Фруктовый отдел, лучший в городе по тропическим фруктам: дуриан, мангостин, чемпедак и крошечные сладкие бананы (писанг эмас), которыми славится Пенанг.

**Rojak** в Пенанге готовится с более тёмным и густым соусом из креветочной пасты, чем в версии из Куала-Лумпура. Местные фрукты: незрелое манго, джамбу-айр (восковое яблоко), папайя, ананас, смешиваются с огурцом и репой, заправляются соусом и посыпаются толчёным арахисом и обжаренным кунжутом. У лотка с рочаком у входа на Пенанг-Роуд к обеденному времени выстраивается очередь, которая извивается за угол. Секрет в белачане: владелец закупает его у конкретного поставщика в Балик-Пулау и самостоятельно обжаривает перед тем, как измельчить для соуса.

Фудкорт в Пулау Тикус небольшой, но качество высокое. Выделяются два ларька.

## Рынок Аир Итам: Рынок на склоне холма

## Ночной рынок Бату Ферринги: Пляжный базар

**Апам балик** на ночном рынке готовят на большой чугунной сковороде. Продавец тонко разливает тесто, посыпает его сладкой кукурузой и дроблёным арахисом, складывает и разрезает на треугольные кусочки. Края получаются кружевными и хрустящими. Середина, мягкая и сладкая. RM 3.

Рынки могут ошеломить при первом посещении. Экскурсия Simply Enak по рынкам Пенанга включает Chowrasta и Pulau Tikus с местным гидом, который знает историю каждого ларька, что лучше всего заказывать, и продавцов по именам. Это самый быстрый способ перейти от растерянности к уверенной дегустации.

初めて訪れる人にとって、市場は圧倒されるかもしれません。Simply Enak Penangの市場ツアーでは、チョウラスタとプラウ・ティクスを、各屋台の歴史、注文すべき最高の料理、そして売り手の名前を顔なじみのように把握している地元ガイドと一緒に巡ります。圧倒されている状態から、自信を持って食事を楽しめるようになるための最も早い方法です。

title: Malaysia's Best Wet Markets (What to Buy and What to Eat)
excerpt: Malaysia's Markets: A Food Lover's Guide Malaysia's markets are not just places to shop. They are where the country's food culture is most alive.

children.text: Malaysia's Markets: A Food Lover's Guide

Malaysia's markets are not just places to shop. They are where the country's food culture is most alive. The wet markets supply the restaurants and hawker stalls with fresh ingredients every morning. The night markets feed entire neighbourhoods with cooked food. The hypermarkets are a modern addition, but even they carry the same local produce and spices that have defined Malaysian cooking for centuries.

For a first-time visitor, the market scene can be confusing. There are different types of markets that operate in different ways. This guide covers the three main categories and tells you what to eat at each.
Wet Markets: Where the Day Begins

Wet markets are morning markets that sell fresh produce, meat, seafood, and prepared foods. They are called "wet" because the floors are constantly hosed down to keep produce fresh and to wash away the fish scales and vegetable trimmings.

Every Malaysian city has at least one major wet market. The most famous are Chowrasta Market in Penang, Pudu Market in KL, and the market in Ipoh's Old Town. These markets open around 6 AM and are most active between 7 AM and 10 AM. By noon, most vendors have packed up.

**What to eat at a wet market:** The cooked food section is where the market regulars eat breakfast. Look for the stalls that have queues of older customers. These are the ones that have been feeding the market community for decades.

At Chowrasta Market in George Town, the asam laksa stall on the lower level has no name and no sign. You find it by following the smell of tamarind and fish broth. The owner starts cooking at 8 AM and is usually sold out by 1 PM. The broth is thick, intensely sour, and packed with shredded mackerel. RM 4.50.

At Pudu Market in KL, the morning hawker section serves some of the best wantan mee in the city. The noodles are springy, the char siew is caramelised, and the wantan dumplings are filled with pork and prawn. The stall at the northern end of the food section has been operating since the 1980s.

At the wet market in Ipoh's Old Town, the breakfast stalls serve Ipoh's famous white coffee and kaya toast. The coffee is roasted with palm oil margarine, giving it a smooth, slightly sweet flavour. The kaya (coconut jam) is made in-house at most stalls.

**What to buy:** Fresh tropical fruit is the best purchase at any wet market. Mangosteen, rambutan, cempedak, and durian are all cheaper and better here than at supermarkets. Let the vendor choose your fruit. They know which are ripe.
Night Markets (Pasar Malam): The Evening Food Scene

Pasar malam (night markets) are temporary markets that set up on a different street each day of the week. They operate from about 4 PM to 10 PM. Each neighbourhood in Malaysia has its own pasar malam schedule.

Pasar malam are different from hawker centres. Hawker centres are permanent and focus on sit-down meals. Pasar malam are mobile and focus on walk-and-eat snacks. The food at a pasar malam is designed to be eaten while standing or walking.
**What to eat at a pasar malam:**

**Apam balik** is a thick pancake filled with sweet corn, crushed peanuts, and sugar. The batter is poured into a round cast-iron mould, the filling is added, and the pancake is folded in half. The outside is crisp, the inside is soft, and the filling is warm and sweet. Look for the stall with the largest queue. RM 2.

**Keropok lekor** is deep-fried fish sausage from the east coast of Malaysia. It is made from mackerel and sago flour, shaped into long rolls, boiled, sliced, and fried. The texture is chewy on the inside and crisp on the outside. It is served with a sweet-spicy chilli dipping sauce. The keropok lekor stall at the KL pasar malam in Taman Connaught is the most famous version.

**Satay** at a pasar malam is grilled over charcoal in full view. The smoke is the signal. Follow it. Chicken and beef skewers with peanut sauce, cucumber, and ketupat. The satay at pasar malam is cheaper than at hawker centres and the grilling is done in smaller batches.

**Fried chicken** (ayam goreng) at pasar malam is coated in a turmeric and rice flour batter and fried in deep oil. The skin is shatteringly crisp. The meat stays juicy because the frying time is short. Buy a piece and eat it while walking.

**Cendol** at a pasar malam is served from a stall with a hand-cranked ice shaver. The ice is fluffier than machine-shaved versions. The coconut milk is fresh. The gula melaka syrup is dark and slightly bitter.

**What to buy:** Pasar malam are also the best place to buy local snacks to take home. Curry puffs, kuih, and dried anchovies are all available in small bags. The prices are lower than at tourist shops.

**The pasar malam schedule:** Each day of the week, a different neighbourhood hosts the pasar malam. The most famous night markets are Taman Connaught in KL (Wednesday, the longest in Malaysia), Batu Ferringhi in Penang (nightly during peak season), and Jonker Street in Melaka (weekend evenings).
Hypermarkets: Modern Shopping, Local Food

Hypermarkets are the modern supermarkets that operate across Malaysia. Giant, Lotus's (formerly Tesco), and AEON are the main chains. They are not traditional markets, but they are useful for first-time visitors.

The food courts at hypermarkets serve local food at low prices. The quality is not as high as at hawker centres, but the food is safe, the air-conditioning is welcome, and you can see photos of every dish.

The dry goods section at hypermarkets is a good place to buy local ingredients to take home. Instant laksa paste, sambal, belacan, and rice flour are all available. The prices are lower than at airport shops and the selection is wider.
The Markets to Know
**KL:** Pudu Market (wet market, morning), Taman Connaught Pasar Malam (night market, Wednesday), Central Market (heritage market, daily).
**Penang:** Chowrasta Market (wet market, morning), Batu Ferringhi Night Market (evening, peak season), Pulau Tikus Market (wet market, morning).
**Ipoh:** Ipoh Old Town Market (wet market, morning), Pasir Pinji Pasar Malam (night market, Saturday).
**Melaka:** Jonker Street Night Market (weekend evenings), Pasar Besar Melaka (wet market, morning).
**Kota Kinabalu (Sabah):** Gaya Street Sunday Market (morning), Sinsuran Market (seafood, evening).
**Kuching (Sarawak):** Satok Market (wet market, weekend morning), Main Bazaar Night Market (evening).
The Bottom Line

Malaysia's markets are the best windows into its food culture. Wet markets show you the ingredients that go into the food. Night markets show you how the food is cooked and eaten by locals. Hypermarkets show you how the country shops today.

Visit a wet market in the morning to see what is fresh. Visit a pasar malam in the evening to eat what locals eat. The combination gives you a fuller picture of Malaysian food than any restaurant meal.

The Simply Enak food tours in Malaysia visit several of these markets and take you to the stalls that the market regulars themselves line up for. A local guide makes the difference between walking past the best stall and sitting down at it.

translations.title: Pasaran Malaysia: Panduan Pencinta Makanan
translations.excerpt: Pasaran Malaysia bukan sahaja tempat untuk membeli-belah. Mereka adalah tempat budaya makanan negara paling hidup. Pasar basah membekalkan restoran dan gerai penjaja dengan bahan-bahan segar setiap pagi.
translations.content_markdown:
**Apa yang patut dimakan di pasar basah:** Bahagian makanan yang dimasak adalah tempat pelanggan tetap pasar bersarapan. Carilah gerai yang mempunyai barisan pelanggan yang lebih tua. Gerai-geri inilah yang telah memberi makan komuniti pasar selama beberapa dekad.

Pasar malam adalah pasaran sementara yang dibuka di jalan yang berbeza setiap hari dalam seminggu. Ia beroperasi dari kira-kira pukul 4 petang hingga pukul 10 malam. Setiap kawasan di Malaysia mempunyai jadual pasar malam tersendiri.

**Ayam goreng** di pasar malam disalut dengan adunan kunyit dan tepung beras dan digoreng dalam minyak yang banyak. Kulitnya rangup sekali. Dagingnya kekal berair kerana masa menggoreng adalah singkat. Belilah sebiji dan makanlah sambil berjalan.

## Pasar yang Perlu Diketahui

Lawatan makanan Simply Enak di Malaysia melawati beberapa pasar ini dan membawa anda ke gerai-gerai yang menjadi tumpuan pelanggan tetap pasar tersebut. Seorang pemandu tempatan membuat perbezaan antara berjalan melepasi gerai terbaik dan duduk di dalamnya.

translations.meta_description: Pasar di Malaysia bukan sekadar tempat membeli-belah. Di sinilah budaya makanan negara ini paling hidup. Pasar basah membekalkan restoran dan gerai penjaja dengan bahan-bahan segar setiap pagi.

translations.title: 寻味马来西亚：市场美食指南
translations.excerpt: 马来西亚的市场不只是购物的场所，更是这个国家饮食文化最有活力的地方。每天清晨，湿货市场为餐馆和小贩档口输送最新鲜的食材。
translations.meta_title: 马来西亚市场：美食爱好者指南
translations.meta_description: 马来西亚的市场不仅仅是购物的地方。它们是这个国家饮食文化最活跃的地方。湿货市场每天早上为餐馆和小贩摊位提供新鲜食材。
translations.content_markdown:
**在湿货市场该吃什么：** 熟食区是市场常客吃早餐的地方。寻找那些排着老年顾客队伍的摊位。这些摊位几十年来一直为市场社区供应食物。

夜市（Pasar Malam）是每周在不同街道摆设的临时市场。它们大约从下午4点营业到晚上10点。马来西亚的每个社区都有自己的夜市时间表。

**炸鸡（ayam goreng）**在夜市裹上姜黄和米粉调制的面糊后，放入深油中炸制。鸡皮酥脆到一碰就碎，因为油炸时间短，肉质依然多汁。买一块边走边吃。

## 值得了解的市场

Simply Enak 马来西亚美食之旅将带您参观其中几个市集，并带您光顾那些连本地常客也会排队等候的摊位。一位当地向导的带领，能让您从路过最佳摊位变成真正坐下来品尝美食。
